d.what: Prepare the text of one screened SEC exhibit for a single reading.
d.how: Use the existing SEC parser, numbered passages and licence screening. Save the source, the effective 2023 GICS reference and the complete prompt.
d.why: Keep each agreement's surrounding terms and schedules available in the same reading.
assume: The summary route accepts one exhibit URL or a date range through the existing SEC discovery and candidate order.
open: Embedded images are recorded as unread. Prompts beyond the existing CLI bound are reported.

d.what: Screen prepared exhibits before dispatch to Codex.
d.how: Verify the Nov 22 prototype hashes and check each frozen KEEP pointer against the same exhibit's extracted text. Record decisions in the batch screening log.
d.why: Send confirmed KEEPs and readable REVIEWs to the reader while retaining the original decision and review reason.
assume: A version-pinned per-batch opt-in can additionally apply the version-4 exclusion gate to frozen KEEPs.
open: Screening and workbook outputs require manual confirmation against the original filings.

d.what: Produce one structured commercial terms summary per agreement, with source evidence.
d.how: Send the saved prompt to the existing ChatGPT-signed-in Codex CLI, save its raw answer and check the response fields before export.
d.why: Preserve agreement boundaries and make the reader's answers inspectable before Excel mapping.

d.what: Map each saved agreement to one row on the Agreement Summary sheet.
d.how: Map reader fields into 16 columns, label source and transaction type in material conditions, and expand the selected GICS code through its official names. Preserve long text in cell notes and the raw response.
d.why: Keep all terms for an agreement together and distinguish percentage from per-unit rates.
assume: The legacy launcher is a separate entry point.
